entities.name: Enûma Eliš
entities.label: Text
entities.summary: Enūma Eliš, meaning "When on High", is a Babylonian creation myth from the late 2nd millennium BCE and the most complete surviving account of ancient near eastern cosmology. It was recovered by English archaeologist Austen Henry Layard in 1849 in the ruined Library of Ashurbanipal at Nineveh. A form of the myth was first published by English Assyriologist George Smith in 1876; active research and further excavations led to near completion of the texts and improved translation.
